title: Avatar
summary: Initial-based person representations with documented naming and a compact overlapping group.
overview: A dependency-free avatar that uses initials so previews need no remote images. The surrounding context supplies the person's name unless the avatar itself conveys otherwise unavailable information.

component.useWhen: Use an avatar as a compact visual reference to a person or organization next to a visible name or in a labeled group.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid treating an avatar as the only source of identity, or making a noninteractive avatar focusable.

examples.title: Initial avatars
examples.description: Compare circular and square shapes at supported sizes; each is decorative beside real identity text in production.

source.html: AMJLRKNS

variants.title: Avatar group
variants.summary: Overlapping member avatars followed by a visible overflow count and one complete accessible group label.
variants.useWhen: Use an avatar group to summarize membership when individual names are available elsewhere or in the accessible label.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid it when every member must be identified or selected directly.
customization: The group carries one accessible label while decorative initials are hidden.
The +2 item states overflow visually; include hidden names elsewhere when they matter.
Overlap uses a canvas-colored ring to keep every circle distinct.

example.title: Project members
example.description: Inspect the grouped label and compact +2 overflow representation.

source.html: AMJLRK+2

anatomy.name: Shape
anatomy.description: A fixed circular or softly square identity surface.

anatomy.name: Initials
anatomy.description: A short visual fallback derived from the display name.

anatomy.name: Context
anatomy.description: Nearby visible text or a group label that communicates the full identity.

accessibility: Hide an avatar with aria-hidden when the person's visible name is adjacent.
Use role=img and an accessible name only when the avatar communicates identity unavailable in nearby text.
Do not put noninteractive avatars in the tab order.
Treat initials as a visual fallback, not a reliable accessible name.
component.responsive: Avatar sizes remain fixed while rows wrap and groups retain controlled overlap.
limitations: Remote images are intentionally excluded from the preview.
The initials algorithm and image-failure fallback belong to consuming application data logic.

provenance.label: Cross-library avatar study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Chip
summary: Compact entity labels with a separately focusable and specifically named remove action.
overview: A dependency-free chip for representing selected filters, people, or compact entities. Static chips remain plain text; removal is a real button.

component.useWhen: Use chips to show compact selected values or entities that benefit from grouping and optional removal.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid chips for status severity, primary actions, paragraphs, or a dense substitute for ordinary links.

examples.title: Entity chips
examples.description: Review static chips as noninteractive list items.

source.html:

variants.title: Removable chips
variants.summary: Selected entities with native remove buttons, precise accessible names, and polite removal feedback.
variants.useWhen: Use removable chips when people can directly remove values from a selected set.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid making the entire chip keyboard interactive; removal belongs to its explicit button.
customization: Every remove button names the specific entity it affects.
Event delegation supports chips removed after initialization.
The polite status confirms removal without moving focus.

example.title: Remove selected filters
example.description: Remove filters with pointer, Enter, or Space and observe the status message.

anatomy.name: Entity label
anatomy.description: The visible selected value or category.

anatomy.name: Optional remove button
anatomy.description: A native button whose name includes the entity.

anatomy.name: List
anatomy.description: A semantic collection when several chips form one selected set.

accessibility: Keep static chips noninteractive and out of the tab order.
Represent a chip collection as a list when order or grouping is meaningful.
Use a native button for removal and include the item name in its accessible name.
Announce removal politely when the visual disappearance is not sufficient.
component.responsive: Chip lists wrap across lines without truncating labels or shrinking remove targets.
limitations: The example removes DOM nodes but does not update application data or restore deleted values.
Input-driven tag creation is a separate composite component.

title: Divider
summary: Horizontal, labeled, and responsive vertical separators for visually distinct content regions.
overview: A dependency-free separator. Decorative rules stay out of the accessibility tree, while semantic separation uses hr or role=separator only when the content structure benefits.

component.useWhen: Use a divider when spacing alone does not make a meaningful boundary between adjacent content regions clear.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid excessive rules that fragment a page or imply structure not present in the document outline.

examples.title: Horizontal divider
examples.description: Review two content sections separated by a native thematic break.

variants.title: Labeled divider
variants.summary: A decorative centered rule with a visible text transition that carries the meaning.
variants.useWhen: Use a labeled divider to introduce a short transition such as Or between equivalent paths.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid giving a decorative rule separator semantics when the visible label already explains the transition.
customization: The pseudo-element rules are decorative and absent from the accessibility tree.
Keep the label short and avoid using it as a substitute for a real heading.

variants.title: Responsive vertical divider
variants.summary: A vertical separator between peer columns that becomes horizontal when the layout stacks.
variants.useWhen: Use a vertical divider between two peer regions that remain visually close in a horizontal layout.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid vertical rules between unrelated regions or when generous spacing already creates a clear boundary.
customization: aria-orientation reflects the wide-screen separator; the visual orientation changes below 32rem.
If assistive orientation must also change dynamically, update aria-orientation with matchMedia.
Source order remains unchanged when columns stack.

anatomy.name: Adjacent regions
anatomy.description: Content whose relationship justifies a visible boundary.

anatomy.name: Rule
anatomy.description: A horizontal or vertical one-pixel separator.

anatomy.name: Optional label
anatomy.description: Short transition text carried separately from decorative lines.

accessibility: Use hr for a thematic break in content.
Use role=separator and aria-orientation for a meaningful non-hr vertical separator.
Keep purely decorative rules out of the accessibility tree.
Do not use a separator where a heading is needed to describe a new section.
component.responsive: Vertical dividers become horizontal when their two-column layout stacks below 32rem.
limitations: The responsive vertical example does not dynamically change aria-orientation; its customization notes describe that enhancement.
Border styles beyond the shared solid rule are intentionally omitted as decorative permutations.

provenance.label: Cross-library divider study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Tooltip
summary: A concise noninteractive description shown on both hover and focus, dismissible with Escape.
overview: A dependency-free tooltip for supplemental text. It never contains actions, appears for keyboard and pointer users, and remains connected to its trigger through aria-describedby.

component.useWhen: Use a tooltip for brief supplemental clarification of a control whose visible label remains understandable on its own.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid tooltips for essential instructions, errors, rich content, actions, touch-only discovery, or information needed before focusing a control.

examples.title: Hover and focus tooltip
examples.description: Hover or focus the button to show its description, then press Escape to dismiss it.

source.html: Move this project out of active lists.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: An existing interactive element with aria-describedby.

anatomy.name: Tooltip
anatomy.description: A noninteractive role=tooltip element containing concise text.

anatomy.name: Positioning wrapper
anatomy.description: A local containing block for simple placement.

accessibility: Show the tooltip on both hover and keyboard focus.
Connect it to the trigger with aria-describedby.
Allow Escape to dismiss without activating or blurring the trigger.
Keep tooltip content noninteractive and concise.
Do not duplicate the trigger's accessible name verbatim.
component.responsive: Tooltip width is capped to the viewport gutter; essential information must still exist outside the tooltip on touch devices.
limitations: The local CSS placement does not detect viewport collisions or port the tooltip to the top layer.
Touch behavior varies, so tooltips cannot be the only source of required information.
Only top placement is included because positional permutations do not change the component contract.

provenance.label: Cross-library tooltip behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.
